platform: Open-source, self-hosted web application; schools may host it on-premise or on a cloud server. Responsive mobile web interface; no official native mobile apps.

distinctive_features.feature: Teacher-centered planning, homework, assessment, and attendance workflows
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: The school-originated design connects everyday teaching work rather than focusing only on administrative records.
Schools can control access at the module-action level to fit local responsibilities and privacy needs.

distinctive_features.feature: Extensible modules, themes, and dashboard hooks
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Schools can adapt the system or build custom workflows using its module framework and open-source code.
A paid license adds 151 maintained queries and 31 commands for schools needing repeatable operational reports.
Translation support and RTL text can help schools serve diverse language communities.
Schools choose infrastructure and data location, while taking responsibility for operations and security.

distinctive_features.feature: Open-source stewardship through a non-profit foundation
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Foundation oversight separates core project stewardship from optional commercial support and hosting.

weaknesses.issue: Self-hosting requires the school to manage installation, hardening, backups, upgrades, and monitoring.
No official native iOS or Android app; mobile access uses the responsive web interface.
No documented push notifications or WhatsApp channel.
Reviewers report that learning the system can be difficult; Capterra ease-of-use score is 3.5/5 from two reviews.
A G2 reviewer reported slow performance and occasional freezing; evidence is limited to one review.
Capterra reviews cite improvement needs in the frontend, finance workflow, and mobile experience.
Older versions have recorded vulnerabilities; security notices have required essential updates.
No documented native statutory reporting package or certified OneRoster, LTI, or Ed-Fi support.
Current core documentation does not show payroll, transport fleet, hostel, fundraising, or enterprise asset management.
Public adoption totals are not available, and the school map is voluntary.

pricing_model_summary: Core software is free under GPL-3.0. Catalyst costs USD $150 per installation annually; hosting, setup, maintenance, and support are quote-based. Schools cover self-hosting costs.
biggest_strategic_gap: Schools needing a managed, mobile-first system with native statutory reporting and broad integrations must supply infrastructure and fill major capabilities through custom work or other tools.
